scenarios: a signed extension adds a provider ext.kit.local: a run pinned to it reaches the extension's address (every request kit-model)
its tool server (the real MCP test server) dies mid-call: UNKNOWN_OUTCOME / EXTERNAL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, never a success
its before_tool hook times out and its after_tool hook exits 9 (both fail open): recorded, not applied, and the run completes its verified change
its command's text is queued as the person's input with provenance extension:kit/annotate
after a kill and restart recovery has nothing to repair and the task is where it was; unloaded, its provider leaves the gateway
audit: IMPLEMENTED-PARTIAL before: an extension manifest carried hooks only; no package could add tools, commands or providers.
proof: Real Core: one extension package routes hooks, tool servers, commands and providers to their existing owners; its crashes and timeouts neither bypass the Core nor corrupt run state.
negative_proof: A manifest cannot declare a server's trust, reads or sites; a configured server of the same name wins.
limitations: A provider is Core-wide while any session has its extension active; commands carry no permissions.

ci.note: every job green on macOS, Linux and Windows on the first attempt; one change carries IMP-EV-0138 and IMP-EV-0225
